newsitem.title: USA: Mattel fined over Barbie doll delays.
newsitem.headline: Mattel fined over Barbie doll delays.

text.p: The Federal Trade Commission Friday said Mattel Inc agreed to pay $146,186 in civil penalties for failure to make timely deliveries or prompt refunds in the sale of its Barbie collectible dolls.

The agreement is part of a settlement involving FTC charges that the toymaker violated its mail and telephone order rule when it failed to ship the dolls or provide delay notices as required by the rule.
The FTC in its complaint said that beginning in 1994, the company received orders for the dolls by mail or telephone but filed to ship them to buyers within the applicable time under the rule.
In addition, the FTC charged that Mattel failed to offer its customers an option either to consent to a delay in shipping or cancel the order.
The consent decree settles those charges but does not constitute an admission of a violation of law.
Filed in U.S. District Court for the central district of California, it requires the court's approval to become binding.
